_readme: Q8 — the tamper-matrix COMPLETENESS registry: MVP-SPEC.md line 168's
mutation enumeration mapped 1:1 onto implemented rows of the Q7 harness.
Checker: crates/antseal-core/tests/tamper_completeness/mod.rs, run from
tests/tamper_matrix.rs (CI lane `tamper-matrix`). Contract for the codes
these rows bind to: docs/testing/error-code-contract.md (D30).
Three kinds of entry, and the distinction is the point:
families[]      — the spec's own rows. Every case is in exactly ONE
of three states: `rows` (implemented row ids),
`pending` (the task that owes it), or `non_row`
(the recorded argument that it can never have a
row). There is no fourth state and no `none`: a
missing row is never silently absent, and a case
in two states at once is an unresolved claim.
The `non_row` state was added by decision D81 and
is constrained: it must name an entry in
non_rows[] whose `collides_with` names a row that
actually claims the outcome, so the discharge is
checked rather than prose. It exists because Q14's
gate is ZERO pending, and a case that can never
land a row would otherwise hold the gate red for
ever. The discharged-case set is pinned in the
checker (EXPECTED_M0_NON_ROW_CASES) as well.
project_added[] — implemented rows the spec's line-168 list does NOT
name. Legitimate (line 168 is illustrative of `every
mutation fails with a distinct error`, not exhaustive
of it) but each needs a recorded justification, so
the 1:1 spec mapping above stays honest.
non_rows[]      — mutations that deliberately will NOT become rows,
with the reason. Recorded so a future contributor
does not `complete` the matrix by adding one and
breaking the harness's distinctness assertion.
Q14's gate condition is ZERO pending. Q18 extends the same structure with
the M2 anchor rows, which are already enumerated here as pending.

spec_source.note: Every family's `spec_quote` is checked to be a literal substring of its milestone's half of that line. The registry cannot drift from the spec without going red, and it cannot contain an invented family.

cases.what: flip one byte of a revealed unit's ciphertext in the bundle — body or tag, the same outcome either way, since the tag covers both

families.spec_quote: altered manifest field — a covered unit's bytes must fail the `fine_root` leaf-range/boundary-path check, a non-covered (`--no-fine-tree`/raw-mirror) unit's bytes must fail `unit_commit`
families.note: The spec splits this family by the single authoritative commitment for the unit's coverage class. Both routes are separate rows. The covered-unit route landed with G19 (crates/antseal-core/src/test_util/tamper_rows_fine_tree.rs): one bit of a covered unit's revealed content is flipped against the known-good opening of G14's golden work, leaving range, cover and boundary path honest so the fault surfaces exactly at the fine_root binding. That resolves the hazard the pending marker recorded, in G's favour: this is the registry row, so R8's same-route mutation through `verify_bundle` must be an R10 property assertion rather than a second row — R's wrapper arm surfaces the inner code unchanged (error-code contract §2) and `check_registry` would refuse the pair.

cases.what: alter a fine-tree-covered unit's bytes; the leaf-range/boundary-path check against `fine_root` must fail

alter a non-covered (`--no-fine-tree` / raw-mirror) unit's signed `unit_commit`; the recomputation over its bytes must fail. Landed on unit 5 of R6's multi-file work — file 2's only normal unit, its file carrying no fine tree, so `unit_commit` is its single authoritative commitment and no second binding can claim the verdict first. The mutation also breaks the manifest signature, and the row still reports the content failure: Files (stage 4) run before Signatures (stage 5).

families.note: Every commitment is salted (project rule 3), so this family has one case per commitment kind; each opens with a bit-flipped salt.

cases.what: flip one bit of the disclosed `unit_salt`
flip one bit of the disclosed `path_salt`
flip one bit of the disclosed `file_salt`, opening `raw_commit`
flip one bit of the disclosed `file_salt`, opening `canon_commit`

families.spec_quote: wrong-length salt or seed (16-B `*_salt`; 32-B `s_root`/GGM seed/boundary node)
families.note: The spec names six length-checked fields: three 16-byte `*_salt`s and three 32-byte values. One case each. Five carry BOTH a C-level primitive row and an R-level pipeline-view row (the `s-root-32` precedent), because the two check different surfaces; `ggm-seed-32` is R-only, per the `crypto-level-ggm-seed-length` non-row. Every R-level row is a DIRECT call on `check_structural`: F8's schema decodes each of these into a fixed-size type, so a wrong-length value never reaches R's group 1 through `verify_bundle` (error-code contract, the 2026-07-28 R5 rider).

cases.what: truncate the disclosed `unit_salt` to 15 bytes
truncate the disclosed `path_salt` to 15 bytes
append a byte to the disclosed `file_salt` (17 bytes)
truncate the disclosed `s_root` to 31 bytes
supply a wrong-length GGM covering seed
append a byte to a boundary Merkle node hash (33 bytes)
decrypt a unit under a different master secret W
present unit A's ciphertext under unit B's entry; the AAD's `unit_id` binding — not a commitment — is what catches it first

families.note: Four named violations, four cases. C14 ratified the per-algorithm codes.

cases.what: delete the ML-DSA-65 signature, leaving one good signature
replace the Ed25519 signature with one by another author
add a valid ML-DSA-65 signature the policy does not list
strip every algorithm from `sig_policy`

families.spec_quote: non-canonical Ed25519 `S` (mauled but strict-invalid) / non-canonical ML-DSA encoding

cases.what: maul the Ed25519 `S` to S + L — same scalar, non-canonical encoding, rejected by `verify_strict`
raise the ML-DSA hint cut above omega = 55

families.spec_quote: non-canonical CBOR body (duplicate key, non-shortest int, indefinite length, trailing bytes)
families.note: Exactly the four the spec names. F3's decoder rejects more classes than these (spec line 153's full RFC 8949 §4.2.1 profile); those rows are in project_added.

cases.what: repeat a map key with a second value
re-encode the value 1 in a two-byte head
re-encode the map with an indefinite-length head
append a byte after the complete top-level item

families.note: Three named violations of the exact-tiling invariant (spec line 121).

cases.what: extend the first unit's range into the second's
extend a unit's range past the file's `size`
delete a unit, leaving a gap in the file's coverage

families.spec_quote: raw-mirror wrongly included in the tiling set

cases.what: replace a file's canonical units with its raw mirror

families.spec_quote: raw-mirror whose `canonicalize(raw)` ≠ the file's canonical bytes

cases.what: substitute raw-mirror bytes that do not canonicalize to the file's canonical bytes
declare a `true_length` that disagrees with the unit's [start, end) width
append one extra 256-byte pad bucket beyond the `padded_length` formula

families.spec_quote: over-broad GGM cover whose node spans an unrevealed real leaf
families.note: Landed by G19 (crates/antseal-core/src/test_util/tamper_rows_fine_tree.rs): the honest single-node cover of [16, 24) is replaced by its parent, which spans real leaves [16, 32) and therefore commits eight leaves the reveal does not show. The substituted node carries its GENUINE s_root-derived seed at a valid grid address, so the only fault is over-broadness and G13 cannot reject it on a length or shape ground instead. The construction helper is `over_broad_cover` in that module — the single one in the workspace. That resolves the hazard the pending marker recorded, in G's favour: R7 consumes that helper for a pipeline-level property instead of registering a colliding row.

cases.what: substitute a dyadically-valid but over-broad GGM cover whose node spans an unrevealed real leaf (spec line 96's leaf-exact-cover rule)

families.note: Split per material because each has its own code (D28, docs/decisions/D28-full-reveal-strictness.md). The symmetric *missing*-material rows are NOT in this family — see project_added; D28 ratified them as a project addition precisely so this mapping stays honest. R7 landed both: the `file_salt` row drives `verify_bundle`; the `s_root` row is a DIRECT call on `classify_file_reveal`, because F8 makes `file_salt` mandatory inside a `full_reveals` entry, so a bundle can never present `s_root` alone and D28 row 1 always claims the pipeline verdict. That unreachability is itself pinned by a test (`the_pipeline_route_to_an_s_root_leak_is_the_file_salt_row`), so the day the bundle schema gains an `s_root`-only shape the row becomes a pipeline row.

cases.what: attach a partially revealed file's `file_salt` to the bundle
attach a partially revealed file's `s_root` to the bundle

families.note: Two fixtures, two errors — an explicit F15 accept (`oversized ≠ over-deep`). Landed at F15 (2026-07-28). No code was minted for either: the size cap's code `bundle-too-large` was already one of F11's eighteen (decision D10 §1 tabled it for exactly this row) and `cbor-nesting-too-deep` has existed since F3, which is why the pending markers recorded one null and one non-null expected code.

cases.what: a body exceeding the hard cap on bundle size / unit count / allocation (spec line 153)
nesting beyond the decoder's depth cap
an otherwise valid `.ots` proof / TSA token committing to a digest other than this seal's `anchor_digest`

pending.why: M2 anchor rows; the code set arrives with A18's anchor verification. Registered now so Q18's extension is a data change, not a schema change.

families.spec_quote: well-formed TSA token from an untrusted root

cases.what: a structurally valid TSA token whose chain does not reach the pinned root store

pending.why: The spec states the outcome inline: an untrusted root does not ERROR, it lands in a specific non-headline verdict state. This is the case Q7's `ExpectedOutcome::VerdictState` namespace exists for.

families.spec_quote: forged Bitcoin header that fails the `--online` block match

cases.what: an OTS attestation whose embedded header does not match the block returned by the online endpoint

families.spec_quote: an `attested` OTS anchor correctly withheld from the offline headline

cases.what: a well-formed `attested` (not yet Bitcoin-confirmed) OTS anchor must not reach the offline headline verdict

pending.why: A positive-shaped row: the artifact is honest, and what is being pinned is that the verdict machine withholds it. A18/R17 own the state names.

families.note: Two cases: LTV semantics mean `expired ≠ invalid` only when the certificate was valid AT genTime.

cases.what: the signing certificate had already expired when the token's genTime claims it signed
the certificate was valid at genTime and expired later — must still verify (LTV)

pending.why: M2; the positive control for the expiry pair — `expired ≠ invalid` (MVP-SPEC.md risks, pinned roots + genTime LTV).

cases.what: a token encoded in BER where RFC 3161 requires strict DER

pending.why: M2; strict-DER limits and their fuzz targets are A/Q17.

project_added.why: Line 168's CBOR family names four cases; the canonical profile the decoder actually enforces is line 153's full RFC 8949 §4.2.1 set, which adds unsorted keys. Kept as a row because a verifier that accepts unsorted keys accepts two encodings of one manifest.
Well-formedness, not canonicality: a truncated head is the commonest hostile-bundle shape and must produce its own code rather than a generic parse failure (spec line 187, hostile bundles).
The v1 CBOR profile forbids floats outright (F1/F3). Not named at line 168; kept because a float slipping through would break the deterministic-encoding claim the whole format rests on.

F15. Line 168's CBOR family names four cases; the profile the decoder actually enforces is line 153's full RFC 8949 §4.2.1 set, which separates a non-shortest *length argument* (bstr/tstr/array/map head) from a non-shortest *integer value* — F3 gives them two variants and two codes precisely so a tamper row can tell them apart. `cbor-non-shortest-int` was already a seed row; this is its length-head twin, mutating the manifest body map's own head. Without it the whole `NonShortestLength` variant would have no row despite being reachable at every container head in both formats.

F15. Line 168 does not enumerate the key-band classes at all — the v1 reserved band is F4's registry rule (§1 rule 4, §7.15), written after that line. It earns a row because reserved and unknown are the two halves of forward compatibility: a v1.x key MUST be rejected by a v1 verifier with a distinguishable code, or a receiver cannot tell `this bundle is from a newer antseal` from `this bundle is corrupt`. Mutation: append body key 8, the body map's first reserved key.

F15, the other half of the same rule: key 24 is above the v1 band and was never reserved, so it can never become meaningful and its rejection is permanent. Distinct code from the reserved arm by design. Also the class F15's line-73 completeness list names as `unknown map key`.

F15. The bundle family's reserved-band row, and deliberately mutated at key 10 — the *named* reserved slot (v1.1 `range_reveals`). Registry §7.15 requires a named slot to raise the **ordinary** reserved-key error rather than its own, because giving it a code would mean v1.1 changes an error code when it assigns the key, which D30 §3 forbids. The row is what pins that: if someone ever gives key 10 a bespoke code, this row goes red.

F15. The bundle-side unknown-key row (key 24). Separate from `manifest-unknown-key` because D78 keeps the two schema families structurally disjoint — `BundleError` has no arm that can carry a `ManifestError` — so `malformed bundle` and `malformed manifest inside a well-formed bundle` must stay two different codes, and a row on each is what proves the split is real rather than conventional.

The second arm of padding integrity. Line 168 names only the over-padded arm (length ≠ `padded_length`); a pad byte that is non-zero at the correct length is a different mutation with its own code, and R7's task text enumerates it explicitly.

R3 structural invariant (spec line 121): a bundle revealing a `unit_id` absent from the signed manifest. Not in line 168's enumeration; R7's task text lists duplicate/unknown unit and file references.
R3 structural invariant: the same `unit_id` revealed twice. Same basis as above.

Substituting a touched file's disclosed path while keeping its salt. Line 168's `altered manifest field` family names only the two unit-BYTES routes, so this path-substitution route is recorded as project-added rather than folded into that family. R8's task text lists it (`wrong path_salt/path → path_commit mismatch`).

Line 168 names four `sig_policy` violations; C14 added a fifth from spec line 97, which requires the policy to be a duplicate-free list of registered algorithm ids. A duplicate is not `empty`, `missing`, `invalid`, or `unlisted-extra`, so it needs its own code.
Sixth `sig_policy` case, same basis: an unregistered/reserved algorithm id (D17 reserves 2–15 and requires rejection). Distinct from `unlisted-extra`, which is a valid algorithm the policy omits.

The fourth tiling violation. Line 168's `non-mirror-range-violations` family names three (overlapping / out-of-bounds / non-tiling), but spec line 121's invariant is `sorted, non-overlapping, and exactly tiling` — R3 checks sortedness as its own pre-pass with its own code, precisely so a descending unit table is diagnosed as unsorted rather than as a gap at the first range. R7's task text lists it.

R3 structural invariant (spec line 121): a `touched_files` entry naming a `file_id` the signed file table has no row for. The unit-side siblings (`unknown-unit-ref`, `duplicate-unit-reveal`) are already project-added; this completes R7's `duplicate/unknown unit and file references`. NOT the D82 shape — that is an EXISTING file with no revealed unit, which has its own row (`verify-touched-file-without-revealed-unit`) and its own code, and fires later: R3's group 3 rejects the dangling reference here before coherence ever runs.

D28's R7 row table, the *missing*-material direction. Line 168 names only the leak direction; D28 ratified strictness in both, so a full reveal that withholds its `file_salt` must fail with its own code — otherwise the two whole-file content commitments would have no verification path at all (D28 §Why strict).

The fine-tree arm of the same rule: a fully revealed file WITH a fine tree must disclose `s_root`. Separate code from the `file_salt` arm because the two materials are independently adjudicated (D28 rows 3 and 4).

D74's direction: EXTRA material. An `s_root` attached to a `--no-fine-tree` file's full reveal is rejected, which is what makes D28's present-set-==-required-set rule total — strip units and the leak arm fires, strip material and the missing arm fires, add material and this one does, so a third party cannot alter a bundle's reveal shape undetected in any direction.

D28 row 7 on a TEXT file: the concatenated non-mirror bytes must open `canon_commit`. Not in line 168's list, and the check has no other verification path — `fine_root` and `unit_commit` are per-unit, `path_commit` per touched file — so without a row the strictness D28 ratified would be untested at the bundle level.
The same check's other arm: a BINARY file's concatenation opens `raw_commit`. Its own code because a verdict must say which commitment disagreed.

D28 row 9. On a TEXT file the concatenation check opens `canon_commit`, so a corrupt `raw_commit` survives row 7 and is caught by the raw-mirror binding instead — the same corrupted field reaching a different code by a different route, which is exactly why both rows exist.

The pipeline-level counterpart of the `over-padded-unit` spec case, whose row (`crypto-padding-length-mismatch`) pins C8's `strip_padding` primitive. R's code is a genuinely different outcome: its payload is recomputed from the manifest's `true_length` in wide arithmetic so the rendered error is byte-identical on native and wasm32 (spec line 169), which only a pipeline row exercises. Uses C9's own mis-encryptor, so the row also proves the padding rejection fires strictly AFTER the AEAD authenticates.
Same basis, other arm: a pad byte that is non-zero at the correct length. `crypto-non-zero-padding` (itself a project addition) pins the primitive; this pins the pipeline verdict.

D80's rule (docs/decisions/D80-revealed-unit-touched-file.md), landed at R5: a revealed unit's file MUST appear in `touched_files`. Not in line 168's enumeration because the rule did not exist when the line was written. Needs both layers decoded at once to observe, which is why R5 was the first task that could.

Decision D82 closes the converse of D80: `touched_files` must equal the set of files with a revealed unit. Not named at MVP-SPEC.md line 168, whose list illustrates rather than exhausts; kept because the bundle is unsigned and `path_salt` is a per-work constant, so without this rule any relay holding another bundle of the same work can splice a genuine `{path, path_salt}` entry into a bundle whose sealer chose not to disclose that file — the D74 add-material hole, in the touched-file section.

R5's reveal-section rule: a unit shipped in the reveal section its SIGNED manifest binding forbids. Named from the bundle's mistake, since that is what a tamper row mutates. Not in line 168's list — it is the check that makes the per-unit stage's dispatch total, so without it a covered unit could be opened by a `unit_commit` the manifest never assigned it.

The other arm of the same rule, and its own code because a verdict must say which direction the bundle got wrong. Exercised with a raw mirror, which is non-covered BY KIND whatever its file's fine-tree state (spec line 94).

D28 row 8 / D75's second route: the disclosed `s_root` must rebuild the manifest's `fine_root`. The row leaves the per-unit cover seeds correct so stage 3 passes and the whole-file rebuild is what fires, making the pair with the cover-seed route (a recorded non-row) a genuine agreement between two independent derivations of `fine_root` rather than one check wearing two hats.

D83: a level == d cover payload's upper 16 bytes are never read as key material, so v1 fixes them at zero and checks them. Before D83 this mutation had NO observable effect — the row was unlandable as written, which is what forced the decision. The fixture flips one bit of byte 16..32 of a leaf-level cover entry in an odd-boundary reveal (n = 6, reveal {2}, node (3,2)).

D77 section 6 names a row for `manifest-empty-normal-units` and F15 deliberately did not take it: `FileEntry::new` refuses to construct a mirror-only file, so the only route is a byte mutation of a NESTED unit's `kind`, which needed F25's span primitive. Not named at line 168 — the enumeration predates D77. Kept as a row because the shape it rejects would leave a file's `canon_commit`/`raw_commit` permanently unopenable, the condition D28 rationale 1 exists to prevent.

One representative of `ManifestError::ListTooLong`, whose two discriminants F11 minted with no row and no named owner (tasks/F.md F22). `Units` rather than `Files` because it is the work-global `DecodeBudget` (D10 section 1), the one cap in the table whose accounting is not a plain per-head comparison. The other discriminant is a named non-row in `antseal_core::test_util::tamper_rows_caps::DELIBERATE_NON_ROWS`. Line 168's enumeration predates the cap constants, so the 1:1 spec mapping stays honest.

The sole `ManifestError::InputTooLarge` code. Its bundle-side twin `bundle-too-large` already has a row (`cbor-oversized`); this is the layer-2 half, and it fails at the manifest ENVELOPE rather than the bundle, so the pair also pins D10 section 5's stage-1 ordering. Synthesized from a recipe: the mutation is a length (MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES + 1), so 16 MiB never enters the repository.

One representative of `BundleError::ListTooLong`, whose ten discriminants F11 minted with no row and no named owner. All ten come from the same `decode_section` cap check on a claimed array count, and `tests/parser_caps.rs` already drives each through the real decode at-cap and cap+1 — so what a row adds (cross-domain distinctness, the no-panic guard, MATRIX visibility) is a property of the error VARIANT, not of the discriminant. `Intermediates` is the representative because `MAX_INTERMEDIATE_COUNT` is 16, the only bundle list cap small enough that a cap+1 fixture can supply all its entries and stay PERFECTLY CANONICAL — which F14's independent cross-check requires of every schema-level fixture, since a document that is also truncated would be rejected by the codec before the schema layer saw it. D10 section 2 separately calls it the weakest-evidence cap in the table. The nine others are named non-rows in `tamper_rows_caps::DELIBERATE_NON_ROWS`.

One representative of `BundleError::ArtifactTooLarge`, whose four discriminants F11 minted with no row and no named owner. `Certificate` because its cap (64 KiB) is the smallest of the four, and F3 refuses an over-claimed `bstr` length before the schema layer sees it — so the bytes must really be present, and a fixture for `ots`/`token` would cost 1 MiB, for `payload` 16 MiB, for the same construct. Synthesized from a recipe. The three others are named non-rows in `tamper_rows_caps::DELIBERATE_NON_ROWS`.

One of six `cbor-` codes F24 found with no row, no fixture and no named owner. The family is structurally unguarded: Q8's registry maps the SPEC's enumeration onto rows, and F23's sweep maps `BundleError`'s and `ManifestError`'s exemplar lists — but the `cbor-` namespace is a third one both of those merely delegate to (`Self::Cbor { source } => source.code()`), so a `cbor-` code is reachable through every schema surface while belonging to neither sweep. Security-bearing: a tagged re-spelling of a value aliasing an untagged one under a single `work_id` is precisely why F3 bans tags. The fixture wraps `full_reveals[0].file_id` in tag 55799 (self-described CBOR) and leaves the value itself unchanged — tag 55799 because it is the one tag a real encoder plausibly prepends on its own, and at layer 1 because `cbor2` applies semantics to known tags, so a tagged embedded body's reachability by the cross-check would depend on which tag number was chosen.

As `cbor-tag`: an unrowed, unowned `cbor-` code, and security-bearing for the same reason — `true`/`null` are not `1`, and the deterministic profile admits neither, so a simple value slipping through would be a second spelling of a value under one `work_id`. The fixture replaces a file's `size` with `true`.

As `cbor-tag`: an unrowed, unowned `cbor-` code, reachable from any `tstr` field. The fixture flips the first byte of `touched_files[0].path` — the disclosed path a user actually reads — to a lone UTF-8 continuation byte. Length-preserving, so every length head in the bundle including the embedded manifest's stays exact.

As `cbor-tag`: an unrowed, unowned `cbor-` code, and load-bearing for D10 section 6's argument that the over-deep row must be a DIRECT call on `check_canonical` — this is the code an over-deep bundle actually produces, because every v1 field has a fixed type and the schema layer's typed read wins at level 1. The fixture replaces a nested unit's `range` array with a byte string of the same width, so the item is perfectly canonical and only the schema's expectation is violated.

As `cbor-tag`: an unrowed, unowned `cbor-` code. Kept as a row rather than a representative-only candidate because a head byte no canonical item can start with is the commonest hostile-input shape after truncation (spec line 187) and the fixture costs one byte. The fixture replaces `touched_files[0].file_id` with a reserved additional-info-28 head — at layer 1 rather than in the body, because F14's cross-check descends into embedded layers only where `cbor2` can load them, and a body carrying a reserved head byte does not load, so the sweep could not confirm it.

non_rows.mutation: drop one revealed unit from a full-reveal bundle **whose file retains at least one other revealed unit**, while leaving `file_salt` attached — the third-party proof-downgrade attack
non_rows.why: Removing a unit reclassifies the file as partially revealed, so the still-attached `file_salt` fires the isolation arm: the observable outcome is `partial-reveal-salt-leak-file-salt`, exactly the same as the row above. Two rows claiming one outcome is a harness failure by design — `check_registry` refuses it, correctly, because the two mutations are one observable failure. The >=2-unit qualifier is load-bearing since decision D82, and R10 measured what actually happens without it. Strip the ONLY normal unit of a file and the outcome depends on whether the mutation RETAINS that file's `touched_files` entry: retained, and the entry is left with nothing revealed, so D82's stage-2 code `touched-file-without-revealed-unit` claims the verdict; dropped — which is what R6's builder does, since it derives `touched_files` from the revealed set — and F8's tier-`[X]` rule `full_reveals` subset-of `touched_files` refuses to CONSTRUCT the bundle at all (`FullRevealWithoutTouchedFile`). So on a single-unit file the downgrade is unrepresentable rather than merely rejected. The mutation stays a non-row on every shape — it collides for one of three reasons, never for none — and the R10 property below is unaffected, because it quantifies over rejection rather than over a particular code.
non_rows.instead: Two R10 properties in `crates/antseal-core/tests/verify_fuzz.rs`: `no_single_unit_deletion_from_a_full_reveal_verifies` sweeps every droppable unit of every file with >= 2 normal units, and `the_single_unit_downgrade_is_unrepresentable` pins the construction-time refusal on the rest.
non_rows.warning: A naive R7 implementation that adds this row will break the tamper harness. That is the harness working, not a bug to route around.

non_rows.mutation: supply a wrong-length GGM covering seed to a C-level primitive
non_rows.why: `CryptoError::SeedLength` carries no kind discriminator, so both 32-byte seeds — `s_root` and the GGM covering seed — bind the single code `crypto-seed-length`, already claimed by the `s_root` row. A C-level GGM-seed row is therefore indistinguishable from it.
non_rows.instead: The R pipeline DOES discriminate (`wrong-length-s-root` vs `wrong-length-ggm-covering-seed`), so the spec's `GGM seed` sub-variant is satisfied by the R-level row `verify-wrong-length-ggm-covering-seed` — registered as pending under family `wrong-length-salt-or-seed`, case `ggm-seed-32`.
non_rows.record: This registry. If a C-level row is ever wanted, the fix is a kind discriminator on `SeedLength` with its own appended code (error-code contract §4), never an edited expected code.

non_rows.mutation: on a fully revealed fine-tree file, replace one GGM cover seed of a covered reveal with a seed that does not descend from the bundle's disclosed `s_root` (decision D75's `the two routes must be required to AGREE` open action)
non_rows.why: D75 kept both routes to `fine_root` — each unit's own leaf-exact GGM sub-cover (R2) and the file's `s_root` (R4) — and left an owed check that they agree. They already do, transitively: a cover seed that does not descend from `s_root` derives different leaf salts, hence different leaves, hence a different folded root, so R2's per-unit binding rejects it as `fine-root-binding-failed`; reaching the signed `fine_root` anyway would be a Merkle collision. The observable outcome is therefore the code G19's pending row already claims, and `check_registry` would correctly refuse the pair. An explicit cover-vs-`s_root` comparison would not help: placed after R4 it is unreachable behind the same fold, and placed before R4 it would displace the spec-mandated `partial-reveal-salt-leak-s-root` verdict on a bundle that both leaks `s_root` and ships an inconsistent cover.

non_rows.mutation: present unit A's ciphertext under unit B's entry in the bundle (MVP-SPEC.md line 168, family `swapped-unit`)
non_rows.why: An AEAD authentication failure is one bit by construction: a single Poly1305 tag comparison covers key, nonce, AAD, ciphertext and lengths, so `decrypt_unit_with_key` can only report `AeadDecryptFailed` and R2 can only report `unit-decrypt-failed` — the same outcome the flipped-ciphertext row claims. Outside the AEAD the verifier holds nothing that separates the two: it never holds `W`, so a bundle-supplied `k_u` is unverifiable; the AAD's `unit_id` binding is an input to the failing check, not an output of it; ciphertext length distinguishes only swaps between different 256-B padding buckets, so it is fixture-dependent rather than a discriminator; and the content commitments that would tell the two apart need a plaintext that does not exist. Decision D81 evaluated and rejected the address-recompute and speculative-re-decryption discriminators.

non_rows.mutation: replace a non-covered revealed unit's bundle-supplied `unit_salt` with another unit's genuinely derived 16-byte salt and verify through `verify_bundle` (tasks/R.md R8's `wrong unit_salt -> unit_commit mismatch` mutation)
non_rows.why: Found at R8; it is D81's argument one commitment layer up. A salted commitment opening is one bit for the same reason an AEAD tag comparison is: the verifier recomputes `SHA-256(0x02 || unit_salt || bytes)` and compares it with the manifest's stored value, and a mismatch says the TRIPLE is inconsistent — it cannot attribute itself to a substituted bundle salt rather than to an altered manifest commit, because both are inputs to the one comparison. `VerifyError::UnitCommitMismatch` carries only `unit_id`, and giving it a cause would mean reporting the result of a sub-comparison that does not exist. The salt is also the right length, so R3's length group cannot claim it first. Note the spec's own `wrong-salt/unit-commit` case is separately discharged by C's primitive-level row `crypto-unit-commit-wrong-salt`, which binds the distinct C code — so a pipeline-level salt row would be a project addition claiming an outcome `verify-non-covered-unit-commit-mismatch` already owns. The manifest-alteration keeps the row because that is the mutation the spec case at `altered-manifest-field/non-covered-unit-fails-unit-commit` names.
